oversized.label: Oversized item

depot.label: Drop-off depot

entries.name: election signs (any material)
entries.note: Election candidates are responsible for removing signs within 72 hours following the day of an election. Please contact the candidate if your sign is not removed. The City offers election sign recycling services at designated Drop-Off Depots for a month following an election. At any other time, place signs made of any material (including corrugated plastic, plastic sleeves and paperboard) and wooden stakes in the garbage. Metal supports can be brought to select Drop-Off Depots as scrap metal.

entries.name: dead skunk
entries.note: If you find a dead animal, contact 311. If found dead on private property, the animal needs to be bagged and placed at the curb for special pickup. You can also make an appointment to bring dead animals to a Toronto Animal Shelter for disposal. If the dead animal is under a deck or porch, please call a private company for animal removal.

entries.name: dead squirrel
entries.note: Do not touch the dead animal with your bare hands. Wear gloves or use a plastic bag to pick it up and put inside two plastic bags (double bag). Then tie the bags closed and place in the garbage. If you find the dead squirrel on City property (e.g. road, sidewalk, park) please contact 311 or double bag it and place it in the garbage.

entries.name: cigar
entries.note: Place this extinguished and cooled item in the Garbage Bin.

entries.name: compostable coffee pods
entries.note: Place this item in the Garbage Bin. The City does not accept coffee pods in its Blue Bin Recycling or Green Bin Organics programs, even if they are labelled recyclable or compostable. Coffee pods can be returned to retailers/manufacturers that have take-back programs.

entries.name: paper cups (cone-shaped)

entries.name: bug spray cans (empty)
entries.note: If container is not empty, dispose of as Household Hazardous Waste. Place this empty, rinsed item, with lid or sprayer on, in the Blue Bin.

entries.name: plastic bug spray bottles (empty)
entries.note: If container is not empty, check if the contents are Household Hazardous Waste and dispose of properly. Place any black and/or compostable plastic in the Garbage Bin. Place this empty, rinsed item, with lid or sprayer on, in the Blue Bin.

entries.name: plastic insect repellent bottles (empty)
entries.note: If container is not empty, check if the contents are Household Hazardous Waste and dispose of properly. Place any black and/or compostable plastic in the Garbage Bin. Place this empty, rinsed item, with lid, pump or sprayer on, in the Blue Bin.

entries.name: sports equipment (balls, gloves, racket
entries.note: Consider donating reusable items to non-profit organizations or bringing to a Community Environment Day. Alternatively, place this item in the garbage.

entries.name: automotive aerosol paints
entries.note: This item is Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) and MUST NOT be disposed of in the garbage, Blue Bin (recycling), Green Bin (organics), drain, toilet or sewer. Take this item to one of the City's Drop-Off Depots or Community Environment Days. For HHW from 10-50 L/kg, you can request a free Toxic Taxi pickup online or by calling 311. In an apartment/condo, building staff need to request pickup.

entries.name: rhubarb leaves
entries.note: Place this item in a kraft paper yard waste bag or rigid open-top container (with an external height between 55 cm and 95 cm, with the exception of blue and grey boxes previously used for recycling). Yard waste in plastic bags or cardboard boxes will not be collected.

entries.note: This type of waste is not accepted by the City of Toronto. Please contact a midwife or hospital to dispose of this item.
